world.setting: Marseille harbour, the Château d'If prison island, Paris salons and bond exchange of the Restoration and July Monarchy, the Monte Cristo grotto in the Mediterranean
world.register: period documentary realism, 1815–1838 France and Italy, candlelit interiors, sea and stone

dantes.name: Edmond Dantès
dantes.role: young sailor, later the Count of Monte Cristo
dantes.look: a lean dark-haired young sailor in his late teens to twenties, sunburnt face, plain sailor's linen shirt and dark trousers, tall and wiry, 1815 Marseille seaman

faria.name: Abbé Faria
faria.role: old priest, prisoner in the next cell, teacher and treasure-keeper
faria.look: an elderly white-haired Italian priest, thin and stooped, ragged black cassock, 1815 prisoner, long untrimmed white beard

danglars.name: Danglars
danglars.role: cold ship's clerk turned banker, the book's bond-market schemer
danglars.look: a stout middle-aged clerk in a dark suit and high white collar, neat side-parted hair, sallow cautious face, 1815 Marseille ship's accountant turned Paris banker

fernand.name: Fernand Mondego
fernand.role: jealous rival who betrays Dantès for Mercédès, later the general Morcerf
fernand.look: a handsome dark-haired young Catalan fisherman in a faded blue jacket, later a Parisian general in a dark military coat with epaulettes

morrel.name: Maximilian Morrel
morrel.role: shipowner's son, loyal friend, nearly takes his own life
morrel.look: a grave young officer in a dark blue naval coat with brass buttons, fair short hair, pale worried face, Marseille shipowner's son, 1815

villefort.name: Gérard de Villefort
villefort.role: ambitious royal prosecutor who buries the letter that sends Dantès to prison
villefort.look: a sharp-faced middle-aged royal prosecutor in a black judicial coat with a white cravat, grey-streaked dark hair swept back, cold precise expression, Restoration France 1815

caderousse.name: Caderousse
caderousse.role: greedy innkeeper and jeweller who sells his friend out for a diamond
caderousse.look: a stooped middle-aged innkeeper in a stained brown waistcoat and loose shirt, unshaven, shifty eyes, rough 1815 Marseille tavern owner

mercedes.name: Mercédès
mercedes.look: a dark-haired young Catalan woman in a simple pale 1815 dress with a shawl, dark eyes, the fiancée of Dantès

monte-cristo.name: The Count of Monte Cristo
monte-cristo.role: Dantès reborn as a mysterious wealthy nobleman with a grotto of treasure
monte-cristo.look: a tall pale aristocrat in his thirties in a black frock coat and white silk cravat, dark hair swept back, cold piercing gaze, 1830s Paris gentleman

marseilleHarbour.look: Marseille harbour at dawn, a three-masted merchant ship moored at the quay, fishing boats, stone warehouses

chateauIf.look: a damp stone prison cell on the Château d'If, a single barred window onto the grey sea, rough walls, a chained iron bed

montecristoGrotto.look: a hidden Mediterranean grotto glittering with heaped gold and jewels in torchlight, faceted granite walls

parisSalon.look: a candlelit 1830s Parisian salon, gilt mirrors, velvet chairs, bankers and counts in evening dress

courtOfJustice.look: a Restoration royal courtroom, dark wood panels, a judge's bench and a prosecutor's table in black robes

bondExchange.look: a Paris banker's office with stacks of bond certificates, ledgers and a brass lamp

spine.claim: Dantès is a young sailor on the verge of captaincy and marriage in 1815 Marseille, and three friends' envy turns his engagement feast into his arrest.
Fourteen years in the Château d'If: Abbé Faria teaches him languages and the map to a buried treasure, and Dantès becomes a man who can plan revenge.
Dantès returns as the Count of Monte Cristo with the treasure and a new identity, and begins to write the fates of his enemies like a banker moves bonds.
Villefort's buried crimes surface, Danglars is ruined by a bond scheme, and Morrel stands at the edge of suicide before the Count's rescue.
The Count's revenge leaves innocents broken and the Count alone with his judgment; the book's final words, Wait and Hope, admit that no one can force absolute justice.
